segments.text: CSS/PMS Group III Optional Subject — Code 25, 100 marks

Town Planning & Urban Management studies how settlements grow, how land and infrastructure are organized, how cities are governed, and how urban development can remain both socially fair and environmentally sustainable. The paper deliberately mixes planning history, the study of urbanization itself, Pakistan-specific planning institutions, urban policy and design, sustainability, and basic spatial-information tools (GIS) — reflecting town planning’s genuinely multidisciplinary character, developed explicitly as the subject’s own first topic.

Clara Greed’s Introducing Town Planning, John Ratcliffe’s Introduction to Town and Country Planning, J. M. Levy’s Contemporary Urban Planning, J. B. Cullingworth and Vincent Nadin’s Town and Country Planning in the UK, and Anthony Townsend’s Smart Cities are the standard reference works behind this syllabus.

items.text: Greed, C. — Introducing Town Planning — core source for the definitional and multidisciplinary material in Unit I.
Ratcliffe, J. — Introduction to Town and Country Planning.
Levy, J. M. — Contemporary Urban Planning — a key source for the urbanization-management material in Unit V.
Cullingworth, J. B., and Nadin, V. — Town and Country Planning in the UK — a standard comparative reference for development control systems, referenced in Unit V.
Townsend, A. — Smart Cities — a key source for the Intelligent Transport Systems and urban-information-systems material in Units V and IX.

segments.text: Note on sourcing: the planning concepts and frameworks in this chapter (settlement hierarchy theory, the sustainability and resilience frameworks, and the GIS/spatial-analysis concepts) are drawn from the standard reference works listed above. Archaeological claims about Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Kot Diji, Mehrgarh, and Gandhara reflect general, well-established findings in South Asian archaeology; any more specific claim about a particular site should be verified against current archaeological scholarship, since interpretation in this field continues to develop. Pakistan-specific planning history (Five-Year Plans, regional plans, master plans) and any current development-authority rule should be verified against official Planning Commission and relevant authority sources before being cited, exactly as this chapter itself repeatedly instructs.
